why: At each minute you need the average of the last precedingMinutes values: a fixed-size window sliding along numCalls. Keep its running sum and compare sum > threshold * window instead of dividing.
hints: Each alert check looks at the same number of consecutive minutes, shifted by one each time.
A fixed-size sliding window: add the new minute, drop the one that fell out. 'average > threshold' is the same as 'sum > threshold * precedingMinutes'.
Sum the first window, then slide n - precedingMinutes times, counting windows whose sum exceeds the limit. O(n), no floats.
pitfalls: The comparison is strict: an average exactly equal to the threshold sends no alert.
No check happens until a full window exists; precedingMinutes = n gives exactly one check.
Avoid integer division of the average (10.33 would become 10).
statement:
A compliance system records numCalls[i], the number of calls in minute i. At every minute where at least precedingMinutes minutes of data exist (including the current one), it averages the calls over the last precedingMinutes minutes. If that average is strictly greater than alertThreshold, an alert is sent.

Return the total number of alerts sent.

Worked example: precedingMinutes = 3, alertThreshold = 10, numCalls = [0, 11, 10, 10, 7].

  • Minutes 0–2: (0+11+10)/3 = 7 → no alert.
  • Minutes 1–3: (11+10+10)/3 ≈ 10.33 > 10 → alert.
  • Minutes 2–4: (10+10+7)/3 = 9 → no alert.

Answer: 1. With alertThreshold = 5 all three windows alert and the answer is 3.
